classification.difficultyReason: Find the constant without a supplied target value by choosing reciprocal conversions, common denominators or expansion, then recognising cancellations that eliminate all angle dependence.

content.prompt: Show that these expressions are independent of $\theta$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{\cos^2\theta}{1-\sin\theta}\\&=\cos^2\theta\cdot\frac{1-\sin\theta+1+\sin\theta}{(1+\sin\theta)(1-\sin\theta)}\\&=\cos^2\theta\cdot\frac{2}{1-\sin^2\theta}\\&=\cos^2\theta\cdot\frac{2}{\cos^2\theta}\\&=2\end{aligned}$$
This is constant wherever the original expression is defined.

$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\tan\theta(1-\cot^2\theta)+\cot\theta(1-\tan^2\theta)\\&=\tan\theta-\tan\theta\cdot\cot^2\theta +\cot\theta-\cot\theta\cdot\tan^2\theta\\&=\tan\theta-\tan\theta\cdot\frac{1}{\tan^2\theta} +\cot\theta-\cot\theta\cdot\tan^2\theta\\&=\tan\theta-\frac{1}{\tan\theta}+\cot\theta-\frac{\tan^2\theta}{\tan\theta}\\&=\tan\theta-\cot\theta+\cot\theta-\tan\theta\\&=0\end{aligned}$$
This is constant wherever the original expression is defined.

$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\tan\theta+\cot\theta}{\sec\theta\operatorname{cosec}\theta}\\&=\frac{\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}}{\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}}\\&=\frac{\dfrac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}}{\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}}\\&=\left(\frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\right)(\sin\theta\cos\theta)\\&=\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta\\&=1\end{aligned}$$
This is constant wherever the original expression is defined.

$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\tan\theta+1}{\sec\theta}-\frac{\cot\theta+1}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta}\\&=\frac{\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+1}{\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}}-\frac{\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}+1}{\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}}\\&=\frac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\cos\theta -\frac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{\sin\theta}\cdot\sin\theta\\&=\sin\theta+\cos\theta-(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)\\&=\sin\theta+\cos\theta-\cos\theta-\sin\theta\\&=0\end{aligned}$$
This is constant wherever the original expression is defined.
